It looks like you don't have a project open yet. Let me explain the most common causes of unnecessary child re-renders: ## Common causes: 1. **Parent re-renders** — If the parent component re-renders, the child re-renders by default. Even if you pass the same prop values, the child will re-render if the parent does. 2. **Props are new object/array references** — If you're creating new objects or arrays in the parent, the child sees them as different props: ```jsx // ❌ Creates new object every render // ✅ Move outside or memoize const data = { name: "John" }; ``` 3. **Inline functions as props** — Passing function callbacks that are defined inline: ```jsx // ❌ New function every render setCount(count + 1)} /> // ✅ Use useCallback const handleClick = useCallback(() => setCount(count + 1), []); ``` 4. **Context changes** — If the child reads from a Context, it re-renders when that Context value changes, regardless of its props. ## Solutions: - **`React.memo()`** — Wrap your child component to prevent re-renders if props haven't changed ```jsx const Child = React.memo(({ data }) =>
{data}
); ``` - **`useCallback()`** — Memoize callbacks passed as props - **`useMemo()`** — Memoize objects/arrays passed as props If you share your code, I can show you the exact fix for your situation.
